newsitem.title: USA: Myriad identifies gene for glioma.
newsitem.headline: Myriad identifies gene for glioma.

text.p: Myriad Genetics Inc and the University of Texas M. D. Anderson Cancer Center said on Wednesday that they have identified the first major gene responsible for glioma, a form of brain cancer that is the leading killer of children with cancer.
The identification of the implicated gene mutated in brain cancer (BNC1) accelerates the development of new diagnostic and therapeutic approaches to this disease.

"The discovery of BNC1 provides solid clues into its possible function for further research into the causes of, and possible treatments for, glioma," said Dr Peter Steck, Associate Professor of Neuro-Oncology, at M. D. Anderson Cancer Center in Houston.
Over 28,000 brain tumors were diagnosed last year in the United States, according to the American Brain Tumor Association.
Brain tumors are known to grow and spread aggressively, compared to many other tumors .

"This discovery demonstrates the potential for our collaboration with M. D. Anderson Cancer Center to make major advances against both brain cancer and leukemia, two important diseases we have chosen for our joint research," stated Peter Meldrum, president and chief executive of Myriad Genetics, a gene discovery and genetic testing company.
